_readme: Hubs for the OpenStreetMap second-hand pull (mapsee_ingest_osm_secondhand.py).
Same shape as osm_food_sources.json: centre + radius_miles, one entry per
metro, tiled by the ingest because Overpass will not serve a 1.45 degree box
in one piece.
THE HUB LIST IS NOT THE FOOD LIST, and that is the point. Measured 2026-08-19
against OSM, the second-hand pool skews UK/EU hard while BUSINESS.md records
fleabop as 'US 140, almost nothing elsewhere'. This supply lands precisely
where that door is currently empty. City-tagged venues with readable hours,
shop=second_hand + shop=charity only:
London 150   Berlin 56   Helsinki 40   Edinburgh 35   Wien 29
's-Gravenhage 29   Cambridge 28   Norwich 28   Bristol 25   Budapest 25
Those counts are a FLOOR. addr:city is present on only 35-39% of the pool and
that is a limit of the counting instrument, not of the data - every element
carries a coordinate, so a 50-mile box picks up the untagged ones too. Expect
a live run to find materially more than the numbers above.
A 50-mile radius around London also swallows most of the south-east, which is
correct for this category: charity shops are a high-street institution and
the interesting density is in the towns, not the centre.
Adding a hub is three lines, and it is cheaper here than for food: this
adapter fetches nobody's website, so a new hub costs Overpass tiles once a
month and nothing else.
The four US hubs are last on purpose. They are the weakest markets for this
category and they are where fleabop already has what little it has, so they
are the least informative place to prove the adapter works.
